!Sample_characteristics_ch1 = treatment: spaceflight
!Sample_growth_protocol_ch1 = Rodent Research Reference Mission 1 (RRR-1) / Rodent Research-8 (RR-8) consisted of 40 BALB/cAnNTac females (8 used for this study) termed Flight which were sent on 12/5/2018 to the International Space Station (ISS), and a control group of 40 mice remained on Earth, termed Habitat Ground Control (HC). Furthermore, two age groups were used, younger (â¼3 months) and older (â¼8 months). Flight mice were housed at double density on launch and again during the return to earth. HC mice were housed to match, as closely as possible, conditions experienced by Flight mice. This included double density housing in identical Mouse Habitat Units and Transporters as used by NASA during launch for Flight mice, and matched temperature, humidity, and carbon dioxide levels (elevated on the ISS compared to Earth) based on actual flight environmental monitoring. HC mice were shipped to Scripps Institute just prior to the return of the Flight mice so that all mice could be dissected together in matching conditions (+/- 1 day). The mice from the Flight group were returned alive to Earth on 1/14/2019 after 39.5 days on the ISS and collected 2-4 days after splashdown following functional assays at Scripps Research Institute. In this study, fresh organ samples were obtained and immediately processed from 8 live mice that arrived at Stanford University from Scripps Research Institute on 1/16/2019. Two mice each from the following groups were included: Flight 3mo, Flight 8mo, HC 3mo, HC 8mo. All four Flight mice were dissected on 1/16/2019 to minimize time spent outside of microgravity, and all four HC mice dissected on 1/17/2019. All mice were adapted to NASA Nutrient Food Bars, four weeks prior to launch, and bars were exchanged weekly. Mice had ad libitum access to both food and water.
!Sample_molecule_ch1 = polyA RNA
!Sample_extract_protocol_ch1 = Peripheral blood samples (0.5 â 1 mL) were collected by cardiac puncture into K2/EDTA-coated syringes and MiniCollect tubes (Greiner Bio-One) immediately after mice were euthanized by CO2 inhalation and cervical dislocation. Red blood cells were depleted with Histopaque-1119 (SigmaAldrich RNBF0417). The cell suspension was then pelleted (300 x g, 4o C, 5 min), filtered through a 70 Î¼m strainer, and resuspended in FACS buffer (2% sterile FBS in PBS) with 100 U/mL DNase I (Worthington LS006344) prior to loading cells on a 10x chromium chip.  Murine eyes were collected carefully using forceps in cold PBS. The whole eyes from each donor were weighed. Subsequently, each of the eyes was dissected under a dissecting microscope to segregate the extraocular muscles, retina, cornea, lens and optic nerve tissue components. Each of these tissues for each donor were digested separately for single cell preparation and pooled together as eye cell suspension. The optic nerves and retina were digested for 15 mins in papain and subsequently resuspended in HBSS solution for mechanical dissociation of single cells by pipetting. The corneal tissue was incubated in Dispase II for an hour with shaking followed by 10 mins of 0.25% trypsin digestion. The corneal cells were then mechanically dissociated using pipetting and resuspended in PBS (with 1% FBS). The lens tissue was processed in 0.02% EDTA for 10 mins and mechanically resuspended into single cells by pipetting. The extraocular muscles were treated with 1mg/ml collagenase for 45mins with pipetting every 15 mins for single cell suspension. All the pooled cells were finally resuspended in 1% FBS containing PBS at a concentration of 106 cells/ml for subsequent processing on 10X.  Femurs, hip bones and vertebral columns were dissected and cleaned of soft tissue. Bones were then processed as previously described (https://doi.org:10.1016/j.cell.2014.12.002, https://doi.org:10.1038/nprot.2018.041). Briefly, bones were crushed using mortar and pestle and subsequently digested in M199 (cat#11150067, Thermo Fisher Scientific) with 2.2 mg ml-1 collagenase II buffer (cat#C6885, Sigma-Aldrich) at 37 Â°C for 60 min under constant agitation. Dissociated cells were strained through a 100-Î¼m nylon filter, washed in staining medium (10% fetal bovine serum (FBS) in PBS) and pelleted at 200g at 4Â°C. The cell pellet was resuspended in staining medium and red blood cells were depleted via ACK lysis for 3 min. After an additional wash step cells were pelleted at 200g at 4Â°C. The single cell suspension was then prepared for fluorescence activated cell sorting (FACS) by staining them with fluorochrome-conjugated antibodies (Thermo Fisher Scientific) against CD45 (cat#15-0451; 1:200), TER119 (cat#15-5921; 1:200), CD51 (cat#12-0512; 1:50), Tie2 (cat#14-5987; 1:20), CD31 (cat#11-0311;1:200), Th1.1 (cat#47-0900; 1:100), Thy1.2 (47-0902; 1:100), 6c3 (cat#17-5891; 1:100), CD105 (cat#13-1051; 1:50) and streptavidinâPEâCy7 conjugate (cat#25-4317-82; 1:100). Target populations were sorted on a FACS Aria II Instrument (BD BioSciences) using a 70-Î¼m nozzle in the Shared FACS Facility in the Lokey Stem Cell Institute (Stanford). 16 Gating of cell populations was guided by appropriate isotype and fluorescence-minus- one controls. Propidium iodide staining was used to separate dead cells. Cells were sorted into staining medium and directly processed for 10X Genomics scRNA-seq.  All other tissues were processed as previously described (https://doi.org:10.1038/s41586-020-2496-1).
!Sample_extract_protocol_ch1 = Single cells were captured in droplet emulsions using the GemCode Single-Cell Instrument (10x Genomics) and scRNA-seq libraries were constructed as per the 10x Genomics protocol using GemCode Single-Cell 3â Gel Bead and Library v3 Kit. Cells were loaded in each channel with a target output of up to 5,000 cells per sample, though fewer cells were captured for small sample types. All reactions were performed in the Biorad C1000 Touch Thermal cycler with 96-Deep Well Reaction Module. Twelve cycles were used for cDNA amplification and sample index PCR. Amplified cDNA and final libraries were evaluated on a Fragment Analyzer using a High Sensitivity NGS Analysis Kit (Advanced Analytical). Library preparation was performed one organ type at a time, in sets of 8 samples. Within each organ set, cDNA was normalized and 13-20 PCR cycles run depending on cDNA amount. The average fragment length of 10x cDNA libraries was quantitated on a Fragment Analyzer (AATI), and by qPCR with the Kapa Library Quantification kit for Illumina. Each library was diluted to 4nM, and equal volumes were pooled for each NovaSeq sequencing run. Pools were sequenced with 100 cycle run kits with 28 bases for Read 1, 8 bases for Index 1, and 91 bases for Read 2 (Illumina 20012862). A PhiX control library was spiked in at 0.2 to 1%. Libraries were sequenced on the NovaSeq 6000 Sequencing System (Illumina).
!Sample_description = Library name: Non-myeloid_Cerebellum-LAR_1_1-Mouse_1-Pool_3
!Sample_data_processing = The obtained reads were mapped to the mm10 reference genome using cellranger (version 5.0.0, 10X Genomics). Ambient cell free mRNA contamination of each sample was removed using SoupX (version 1.5.2). Samples with more than 10% estimated contamination were removed. Raw gene counts were loaded into Seurat (version 4.0.3) for further processing. Cells with less than 200 or more than 2500 features, as well as cells with more than 50% mitochondrial RNA were removed. Samples with less than 50 cells were removed from the dataset. Finally, doublets were removed using DoubletFinder (version 2.0.3).

!Sample_title = Non, myeloid Cerebellum, LAR, Mouse 4
!Sample_geo_accession = GSM8947932
!Sample_status = Public on Dec 18 2025
!Sample_submission_date = Apr 23 2025
!Sample_last_update_date = Apr 22 2026
!Sample_type = SRA
!Sample_channel_count = 1
!Sample_source_name_ch1 = Non-myeloid_Cerebellum
!Sample_organism_ch1 = Mus musculus
!Sample_taxid_ch1 = 10090
!Sample_characteristics_ch1 = strain: BALB/cAnNTac
!Sample_characteristics_ch1 = Sex: female
!Sample_characteristics_ch1 = batch: Pool 3
!Sample_characteristics_ch1 = tissue: Non-myeloid_Cerebellum
!Sample_characteristics_ch1 = age: 8
!Sample_characteristics_ch1 = treatment: spaceflight
!Sample_growth_protocol_ch1 = Rodent Research Reference Mission 1 (RRR-1) / Rodent Research-8 (RR-8) consisted of 40 BALB/cAnNTac females (8 used for this study) termed Flight which were sent on 12/5/2018 to the International Space Station (ISS), and a control group of 40 mice remained on Earth, termed Habitat Ground Control (HC). Furthermore, two age groups were used, younger (â¼3 months) and older (â¼8 months). Flight mice were housed at double density on launch and again during the return to earth. HC mice were housed to match, as closely as possible, conditions experienced by Flight mice. This included double density housing in identical Mouse Habitat Units and Transporters as used by NASA during launch for Flight mice, and matched temperature, humidity, and carbon dioxide levels (elevated on the ISS compared to Earth) based on actual flight environmental monitoring. HC mice were shipped to Scripps Institute just prior to the return of the Flight mice so that all mice could be dissected together in matching conditions (+/- 1 day). The mice from the Flight group were returned alive to Earth on 1/14/2019 after 39.5 days on the ISS and collected 2-4 days after splashdown following functional assays at Scripps Research Institute. In this study, fresh organ samples were obtained and immediately processed from 8 live mice that arrived at Stanford University from Scripps Research Institute on 1/16/2019. Two mice each from the following groups were included: Flight 3mo, Flight 8mo, HC 3mo, HC 8mo. All four Flight mice were dissected on 1/16/2019 to minimize time spent outside of microgravity, and all four HC mice dissected on 1/17/2019. All mice were adapted to NASA Nutrient Food Bars, four weeks prior to launch, and bars were exchanged weekly. Mice had ad libitum access to both food and water.
!Sample_molecule_ch1 = polyA RNA
!Sample_extract_protocol_ch1 = Peripheral blood samples (0.5 â 1 mL) were collected by cardiac puncture into K2/EDTA-coated syringes and MiniCollect tubes (Greiner Bio-One) immediately after mice were euthanized by CO2 inhalation and cervical dislocation. Red blood cells were depleted with Histopaque-1119 (SigmaAldrich RNBF0417). The cell suspension was then pelleted (300 x g, 4o C, 5 min), filtered through a 70 Î¼m strainer, and resuspended in FACS buffer (2% sterile FBS in PBS) with 100 U/mL DNase I (Worthington LS006344) prior to loading cells on a 10x chromium chip.  Murine eyes were collected carefully using forceps in cold PBS. The whole eyes from each donor were weighed. Subsequently, each of the eyes was dissected under a dissecting microscope to segregate the extraocular muscles, retina, cornea, lens and optic nerve tissue components. Each of these tissues for each donor were digested separately for single cell preparation and pooled together as eye cell suspension. The optic nerves and retina were digested for 15 mins in papain and subsequently resuspended in HBSS solution for mechanical dissociation of single cells by pipetting. The corneal tissue was incubated in Dispase II for an hour with shaking followed by 10 mins of 0.25% trypsin digestion. The corneal cells were then mechanically dissociated using pipetting and resuspended in PBS (with 1% FBS). The lens tissue was processed in 0.02% EDTA for 10 mins and mechanically resuspended into single cells by pipetting. The extraocular muscles were treated with 1mg/ml collagenase for 45mins with pipetting every 15 mins for single cell suspension. All the pooled cells were finally resuspended in 1% FBS containing PBS at a concentration of 106 cells/ml for subsequent processing on 10X.  Femurs, hip bones and vertebral columns were dissected and cleaned of soft tissue. Bones were then processed as previously described (https://doi.org:10.1016/j.cell.2014.12.002, https://doi.org:10.1038/nprot.2018.041). Briefly, bones were crushed using mortar and pestle and subsequently digested in M199 (cat#11150067, Thermo Fisher Scientific) with 2.2 mg ml-1 collagenase II buffer (cat#C6885, Sigma-Aldrich) at 37 Â°C for 60 min under constant agitation. Dissociated cells were strained through a 100-Î¼m nylon filter, washed in staining medium (10% fetal bovine serum (FBS) in PBS) and pelleted at 200g at 4Â°C. The cell pellet was resuspended in staining medium and red blood cells were depleted via ACK lysis for 3 min. After an additional wash step cells were pelleted at 200g at 4Â°C. The single cell suspension was then prepared for fluorescence activated cell sorting (FACS) by staining them with fluorochrome-conjugated antibodies (Thermo Fisher Scientific) against CD45 (cat#15-0451; 1:200), TER119 (cat#15-5921; 1:200), CD51 (cat#12-0512; 1:50), Tie2 (cat#14-5987; 1:20), CD31 (cat#11-0311;1:200), Th1.1 (cat#47-0900; 1:100), Thy1.2 (47-0902; 1:100), 6c3 (cat#17-5891; 1:100), CD105 (cat#13-1051; 1:50) and streptavidinâPEâCy7 conjugate (cat#25-4317-82; 1:100). Target populations were sorted on a FACS Aria II Instrument (BD BioSciences) using a 70-Î¼m nozzle in the Shared FACS Facility in the Lokey Stem Cell Institute (Stanford). 16 Gating of cell populations was guided by appropriate isotype and fluorescence-minus- one controls. Propidium iodide staining was used to separate dead cells. Cells were sorted into staining medium and directly processed for 10X Genomics scRNA-seq.  All other tissues were processed as previously described (https://doi.org:10.1038/s41586-020-2496-1).
!Sample_extract_protocol_ch1 = Single cells were captured in droplet emulsions using the GemCode Single-Cell Instrument (10x Genomics) and scRNA-seq libraries were constructed as per the 10x Genomics protocol using GemCode Single-Cell 3â Gel Bead and Library v3 Kit. Cells were loaded in each channel with a target output of up to 5,000 cells per sample, though fewer cells were captured for small sample types. All reactions were performed in the Biorad C1000 Touch Thermal cycler with 96-Deep Well Reaction Module. Twelve cycles were used for cDNA amplification and sample index PCR. Amplified cDNA and final libraries were evaluated on a Fragment Analyzer using a High Sensitivity NGS Analysis Kit (Advanced Analytical). Library preparation was performed one organ type at a time, in sets of 8 samples. Within each organ set, cDNA was normalized and 13-20 PCR cycles run depending on cDNA amount. The average fragment length of 10x cDNA libraries was quantitated on a Fragment Analyzer (AATI), and by qPCR with the Kapa Library Quantification kit for Illumina. Each library was diluted to 4nM, and equal volumes were pooled for each NovaSeq sequencing run. Pools were sequenced with 100 cycle run kits with 28 bases for Read 1, 8 bases for Index 1, and 91 bases for Read 2 (Illumina 20012862). A PhiX control library was spiked in at 0.2 to 1%. Libraries were sequenced on the NovaSeq 6000 Sequencing System (Illumina).
!Sample_description = Library name: Non-myeloid_Cerebellum-LAR_1_1-Mouse_4-Pool_3
!Sample_data_processing = The obtained reads were mapped to the mm10 reference genome using cellranger (version 5.0.0, 10X Genomics). Ambient cell free mRNA contamination of each sample was removed using SoupX (version 1.5.2). Samples with more than 10% estimated contamination were removed. Raw gene counts were loaded into Seurat (version 4.0.3) for further processing. Cells with less than 200 or more than 2500 features, as well as cells with more than 50% mitochondrial RNA were removed. Samples with less than 50 cells were removed from the dataset. Finally, doublets were removed using DoubletFinder (version 2.0.3).

!Sample_growth_protocol_ch1 = Rodent Research Reference Mission 1 (RRR-1) / Rodent Research-8 (RR-8) consisted of 40 BALB/cAnNTac females (8 used for this study) termed Flight which were sent on 12/5/2018 to the International Space Station (ISS), and a control group of 40 mice remained on Earth, termed Habitat Ground Control (HC). Furthermore, two age groups were used, younger (â¼3 months) and older (â¼8 months). Flight mice were housed at double density on launch and again during the return to earth. HC mice were housed to match, as closely as possible, conditions experienced by Flight mice. This included double density housing in identical Mouse Habitat Units and Transporters as used by NASA during launch for Flight mice, and matched temperature, humidity, and carbon dioxide levels (elevated on the ISS compared to Earth) based on actual flight environmental monitoring. HC mice were shipped to Scripps Institute just prior to the return of the Flight mice so that all mice could be dissected together in matching conditions (+/- 1 day). The mice from the Flight group were returned alive to Earth on 1/14/2019 after 39.5 days on the ISS and collected 2-4 days after splashdown following functional assays at Scripps Research Institute. In this study, fresh organ samples were obtained and immediately processed from 8 live mice that arrived at Stanford University from Scripps Research Institute on 1/16/2019. Two mice each from the following groups were included: Flight 3mo, Flight 8mo, HC 3mo, HC 8mo. All four Flight mice were dissected on 1/16/2019 to minimize time spent outside of microgravity, and all four HC mice dissected on 1/17/2019. All mice were adapted to NASA Nutrient Food Bars, four weeks prior to launch, and bars were exchanged weekly. Mice had ad libitum access to both food and water.
!Sample_molecule_ch1 = polyA RNA
!Sample_extract_protocol_ch1 = Peripheral blood samples (0.5 â 1 mL) were collected by cardiac puncture into K2/EDTA-coated syringes and MiniCollect tubes (Greiner Bio-One) immediately after mice were euthanized by CO2 inhalation and cervical dislocation. Red blood cells were depleted with Histopaque-1119 (SigmaAldrich RNBF0417). The cell suspension was then pelleted (300 x g, 4o C, 5 min), filtered through a 70 Î¼m strainer, and resuspended in FACS buffer (2% sterile FBS in PBS) with 100 U/mL DNase I (Worthington LS006344) prior to loading cells on a 10x chromium chip.  Murine eyes were collected carefully using forceps in cold PBS. The whole eyes from each donor were weighed. Subsequently, each of the eyes was dissected under a dissecting microscope to segregate the extraocular muscles, retina, cornea, lens and optic nerve tissue components. Each of these tissues for each donor were digested separately for single cell preparation and pooled together as eye cell suspension. The optic nerves and retina were digested for 15 mins in papain and subsequently resuspended in HBSS solution for mechanical dissociation of single cells by pipetting. The corneal tissue was incubated in Dispase II for an hour with shaking followed by 10 mins of 0.25% trypsin digestion. The corneal cells were then mechanically dissociated using pipetting and resuspended in PBS (with 1% FBS). The lens tissue was processed in 0.02% EDTA for 10 mins and mechanically resuspended into single cells by pipetting. The extraocular muscles were treated with 1mg/ml collagenase for 45mins with pipetting every 15 mins for single cell suspension. All the pooled cells were finally resuspended in 1% FBS containing PBS at a concentration of 106 cells/ml for subsequent processing on 10X.  Femurs, hip bones and vertebral columns were dissected and cleaned of soft tissue. Bones were then processed as previously described (https://doi.org:10.1016/j.cell.2014.12.002, https://doi.org:10.1038/nprot.2018.041). Briefly, bones were crushed using mortar and pestle and subsequently digested in M199 (cat#11150067, Thermo Fisher Scientific) with 2.2 mg ml-1 collagenase II buffer (cat#C6885, Sigma-Aldrich) at 37 Â°C for 60 min under constant agitation. Dissociated cells were strained through a 100-Î¼m nylon filter, washed in staining medium (10% fetal bovine serum (FBS) in PBS) and pelleted at 200g at 4Â°C. The cell pellet was resuspended in staining medium and red blood cells were depleted via ACK lysis for 3 min. After an additional wash step cells were pelleted at 200g at 4Â°C. The single cell suspension was then prepared for fluorescence activated cell sorting (FACS) by staining them with fluorochrome-conjugated antibodies (Thermo Fisher Scientific) against CD45 (cat#15-0451; 1:200), TER119 (cat#15-5921; 1:200), CD51 (cat#12-0512; 1:50), Tie2 (cat#14-5987; 1:20), CD31 (cat#11-0311;1:200), Th1.1 (cat#47-0900; 1:100), Thy1.2 (47-0902; 1:100), 6c3 (cat#17-5891; 1:100), CD105 (cat#13-1051; 1:50) and streptavidinâPEâCy7 conjugate (cat#25-4317-82; 1:100). Target populations were sorted on a FACS Aria II Instrument (BD BioSciences) using a 70-Î¼m nozzle in the Shared FACS Facility in the Lokey Stem Cell Institute (Stanford). 16 Gating of cell populations was guided by appropriate isotype and fluorescence-minus- one controls. Propidium iodide staining was used to separate dead cells. Cells were sorted into staining medium and directly processed for 10X Genomics scRNA-seq.  All other tissues were processed as previously described (https://doi.org:10.1038/s41586-020-2496-1).
!Sample_extract_protocol_ch1 = Single cells were captured in droplet emulsions using the GemCode Single-Cell Instrument (10x Genomics) and scRNA-seq libraries were constructed as per the 10x Genomics protocol using GemCode Single-Cell 3â Gel Bead and Library v3 Kit. Cells were loaded in each channel with a target output of up to 5,000 cells per sample, though fewer cells were captured for small sample types. All reactions were performed in the Biorad C1000 Touch Thermal cycler with 96-Deep Well Reaction Module. Twelve cycles were used for cDNA amplification and sample index PCR. Amplified cDNA and final libraries were evaluated on a Fragment Analyzer using a High Sensitivity NGS Analysis Kit (Advanced Analytical). Library preparation was performed one organ type at a time, in sets of 8 samples. Within each organ set, cDNA was normalized and 13-20 PCR cycles run depending on cDNA amount. The average fragment length of 10x cDNA libraries was quantitated on a Fragment Analyzer (AATI), and by qPCR with the Kapa Library Quantification kit for Illumina. Each library was diluted to 4nM, and equal volumes were pooled for each NovaSeq sequencing run. Pools were sequenced with 100 cycle run kits with 28 bases for Read 1, 8 bases for Index 1, and 91 bases for Read 2 (Illumina 20012862). A PhiX control library was spiked in at 0.2 to 1%. Libraries were sequenced on the NovaSeq 6000 Sequencing System (Illumina).

The average fragment length of 10x cDNA libraries was quantitated on a Fragment Analyzer (AATI), and by qPCR with the Kapa Library Quantification kit for Illumina. Each library was diluted to 4nM, and equal volumes were pooled for each NovaSeq sequencing run. Pools were sequenced with 100 cycle run kits with 28 bases for Read 1, 8 bases for Index 1, and 91 bases for Read 2 (Illumina 20012862). A PhiX control library was spiked in at 0.2 to 1%. Libraries were sequenced on the NovaSeq 6000 Sequencing System (Illumina).
!Sample_description = Library name: Non-myeloid_Forebrain-LAR_1_3-Mouse_1-Pool_2
!Sample_data_processing = The obtained reads were mapped to the mm10 reference genome using cellranger (version 5.0.0, 10X Genomics). Ambient cell free mRNA contamination of each sample was removed using SoupX (version 1.5.2). Samples with more than 10% estimated contamination were removed. Raw gene counts were loaded into Seurat (version 4.0.3) for further processing. Cells with less than 200 or more than 2500 features, as well as cells with more than 50% mitochondrial RNA were removed. Samples with less than 50 cells were removed from the dataset. Finally, doublets were removed using DoubletFinder (version 2.0.3).

!Sample_growth_protocol_ch1 = Rodent Research Reference Mission 1 (RRR-1) / Rodent Research-8 (RR-8) consisted of 40 BALB/cAnNTac females (8 used for this study) termed Flight which were sent on 12/5/2018 to the International Space Station (ISS), and a control group of 40 mice remained on Earth, termed Habitat Ground Control (HC). Furthermore, two age groups were used, younger (â¼3 months) and older (â¼8 months). Flight mice were housed at double density on launch and again during the return to earth. HC mice were housed to match, as closely as possible, conditions experienced by Flight mice. This included double density housing in identical Mouse Habitat Units and Transporters as used by NASA during launch for Flight mice, and matched temperature, humidity, and carbon dioxide levels (elevated on the ISS compared to Earth) based on actual flight environmental monitoring. HC mice were shipped to Scripps Institute just prior to the return of the Flight mice so that all mice could be dissected together in matching conditions (+/- 1 day). The mice from the Flight group were returned alive to Earth on 1/14/2019 after 39.5 days on the ISS and collected 2-4 days after splashdown following functional assays at Scripps Research Institute. In this study, fresh organ samples were obtained and immediately processed from 8 live mice that arrived at Stanford University from Scripps Research Institute on 1/16/2019. Two mice each from the following groups were included: Flight 3mo, Flight 8mo, HC 3mo, HC 8mo. All four Flight mice were dissected on 1/16/2019 to minimize time spent outside of microgravity, and all four HC mice dissected on 1/17/2019. All mice were adapted to NASA Nutrient Food Bars, four weeks prior to launch, and bars were exchanged weekly. Mice had ad libitum access to both food and water.
!Sample_molecule_ch1 = polyA RNA
!Sample_extract_protocol_ch1 = Peripheral blood samples (0.5 â 1 mL) were collected by cardiac puncture into K2/EDTA-coated syringes and MiniCollect tubes (Greiner Bio-One) immediately after mice were euthanized by CO2 inhalation and cervical dislocation. Red blood cells were depleted with Histopaque-1119 (SigmaAldrich RNBF0417). The cell suspension was then pelleted (300 x g, 4o C, 5 min), filtered through a 70 Î¼m strainer, and resuspended in FACS buffer (2% sterile FBS in PBS) with 100 U/mL DNase I (Worthington LS006344) prior to loading cells on a 10x chromium chip.  Murine eyes were collected carefully using forceps in cold PBS. The whole eyes from each donor were weighed. Subsequently, each of the eyes was dissected under a dissecting microscope to segregate the extraocular muscles, retina, cornea, lens and optic nerve tissue components. Each of these tissues for each donor were digested separately for single cell preparation and pooled together as eye cell suspension. The optic nerves and retina were digested for 15 mins in papain and subsequently resuspended in HBSS solution for mechanical dissociation of single cells by pipetting. The corneal tissue was incubated in Dispase II for an hour with shaking followed by 10 mins of 0.25% trypsin digestion. The corneal cells were then mechanically dissociated using pipetting and resuspended in PBS (with 1% FBS). The lens tissue was processed in 0.02% EDTA for 10 mins and mechanically resuspended into single cells by pipetting. The extraocular muscles were treated with 1mg/ml collagenase for 45mins with pipetting every 15 mins for single cell suspension. All the pooled cells were finally resuspended in 1% FBS containing PBS at a concentration of 106 cells/ml for subsequent processing on 10X.  Femurs, hip bones and vertebral columns were dissected and cleaned of soft tissue. Bones were then processed as previously described (https://doi.org:10.1016/j.cell.2014.12.002, https://doi.org:10.1038/nprot.2018.041). Briefly, bones were crushed using mortar and pestle and subsequently digested in M199 (cat#11150067, Thermo Fisher Scientific) with 2.2 mg ml-1 collagenase II buffer (cat#C6885, Sigma-Aldrich) at 37 Â°C for 60 min under constant agitation. Dissociated cells were strained through a 100-Î¼m nylon filter, washed in staining medium (10% fetal bovine serum (FBS) in PBS) and pelleted at 200g at 4Â°C. The cell pellet was resuspended in staining medium and red blood cells were depleted via ACK lysis for 3 min. After an additional wash step cells were pelleted at 200g at 4Â°C. The single cell suspension was then prepared for fluorescence activated cell sorting (FACS) by staining them with fluorochrome-conjugated antibodies (Thermo Fisher Scientific) against CD45 (cat#15-0451; 1:200), TER119 (cat#15-5921; 1:200), CD51 (cat#12-0512; 1:50), Tie2 (cat#14-5987; 1:20), CD31 (cat#11-0311;1:200), Th1.1 (cat#47-0900; 1:100), Thy1.2 (47-0902; 1:100), 6c3 (cat#17-5891; 1:100), CD105 (cat#13-1051; 1:50) and streptavidinâPEâCy7 conjugate (cat#25-4317-82; 1:100). Target populations were sorted on a FACS Aria II Instrument (BD BioSciences) using a 70-Î¼m nozzle in the Shared FACS Facility in the Lokey Stem Cell Institute (Stanford). 16 Gating of cell populations was guided by appropriate isotype and fluorescence-minus- one controls. Propidium iodide staining was used to separate dead cells. Cells were sorted into staining medium and directly processed for 10X Genomics scRNA-seq.  All other tissues were processed as previously described (https://doi.org:10.1038/s41586-020-2496-1).

!Sample_extract_protocol_ch1 = Single cells were captured in droplet emulsions using the GemCode Single-Cell Instrument (10x Genomics) and scRNA-seq libraries were constructed as per the 10x Genomics protocol using GemCode Single-Cell 3â Gel Bead and Library v3 Kit. !Sample_growth_protocol_ch1 = Rodent Research Reference Mission 1 (RRR-1) / Rodent Research-8 (RR-8) consisted of 40 BALB/cAnNTac females (8 used for this study) termed Flight which were sent on 12/5/2018 to the International Space Station (ISS), and a control group of 40 mice remained on Earth, termed Habitat Ground Control (HC). Furthermore, two age groups were used, younger (â¼3 months) and older (â¼8 months). Flight mice were housed at double density on launch and again during the return to earth. HC mice were housed to match, as closely as possible, conditions experienced by Flight mice. This included double density housing in identical Mouse Habitat Units and Transporters as used by NASA during launch for Flight mice, and matched temperature, humidity, and carbon dioxide levels (elevated on the ISS compared to Earth) based on actual flight environmental monitoring. HC mice were shipped to Scripps Institute just prior to the return of the Flight mice so that all mice could be dissected together in matching conditions (+/- 1 day). The mice from the Flight group were returned alive to Earth on 1/14/2019 after 39.5 days on the ISS and collected 2-4 days after splashdown following functional assays at Scripps Research Institute. In this study, fresh organ samples were obtained and immediately processed from 8 live mice that arrived at Stanford University from Scripps Research Institute on 1/16/2019. Two mice each from the following groups were included: Flight 3mo, Flight 8mo, HC 3mo, HC 8mo. All four Flight mice were dissected on 1/16/2019 to minimize time spent outside of microgravity, and all four HC mice dissected on 1/17/2019. All mice were adapted to NASA Nutrient Food Bars, four weeks prior to launch, and bars were exchanged weekly. Mice had ad libitum access to both food and water.
!Sample_molecule_ch1 = polyA RNA
!Sample_extract_protocol_ch1 = Peripheral blood samples (0.5 â 1 mL) were collected by cardiac puncture into K2/EDTA-coated syringes and MiniCollect tubes (Greiner Bio-One) immediately after mice were euthanized by CO2 inhalation and cervical dislocation. Red blood cells were depleted with Histopaque-1119 (SigmaAldrich RNBF0417). The cell suspension was then pelleted (300 x g, 4o C, 5 min), filtered through a 70 Î¼m strainer, and resuspended in FACS buffer (2% sterile FBS in PBS) with 100 U/mL DNase I (Worthington LS006344) prior to loading cells on a 10x chromium chip.  Murine eyes were collected carefully using forceps in cold PBS. The whole eyes from each donor were weighed. Subsequently, each of the eyes was dissected under a dissecting microscope to segregate the extraocular muscles, retina, cornea, lens and optic nerve tissue components. Each of these tissues for each donor were digested separately for single cell preparation and pooled together as eye cell suspension. The optic nerves and retina were digested for 15 mins in papain and subsequently resuspended in HBSS solution for mechanical dissociation of single cells by pipetting. The corneal tissue was incubated in Dispase II for an hour with shaking followed by 10 mins of 0.25% trypsin digestion. The corneal cells were then mechanically dissociated using pipetting and resuspended in PBS (with 1% FBS). The lens tissue was processed in 0.02% EDTA for 10 mins and mechanically resuspended into single cells by pipetting. The extraocular muscles were treated with 1mg/ml collagenase for 45mins with pipetting every 15 mins for single cell suspension. All the pooled cells were finally resuspended in 1% FBS containing PBS at a concentration of 106 cells/ml for subsequent processing on 10X.  Femurs, hip bones and vertebral columns were dissected and cleaned of soft tissue. Bones were then processed as previously described (https://doi.org:10.1016/j.cell.2014.12.002, https://doi.org:10.1038/nprot.2018.041). Briefly, bones were crushed using mortar and pestle and subsequently digested in M199 (cat#11150067, Thermo Fisher Scientific) with 2.2 mg ml-1 collagenase II buffer (cat#C6885, Sigma-Aldrich) at 37 Â°C for 60 min under constant agitation. Dissociated cells were strained through a 100-Î¼m nylon filter, washed in staining medium (10% fetal bovine serum (FBS) in PBS) and pelleted at 200g at 4Â°C. The cell pellet was resuspended in staining medium and red blood cells were depleted via ACK lysis for 3 min. After an additional wash step cells were pelleted at 200g at 4Â°C. !Sample_extract_protocol_ch1 = Single cells were captured in droplet emulsions using the GemCode Single-Cell Instrument (10x Genomics) and scRNA-seq libraries were constructed as per the 10x Genomics protocol using GemCode Single-Cell 3â Gel Bead and Library v3 Kit. !Sample_growth_protocol_ch1 = Rodent Research Reference Mission 1 (RRR-1) / Rodent Research-8 (RR-8) consisted of 40 BALB/cAnNTac females (8 used for this study) termed Flight which were sent on 12/5/2018 to the International Space Station (ISS), and a control group of 40 mice remained on Earth, termed Habitat Ground Control (HC). Furthermore, two age groups were used, younger (â¼3 months) and older (â¼8 months). Flight mice were housed at double density on launch and again during the return to earth. HC mice were housed to match, as closely as possible, conditions experienced by Flight mice. This included double density housing in identical Mouse Habitat Units and Transporters as used by NASA during launch for Flight mice, and matched temperature, humidity, and carbon dioxide levels (elevated on the ISS compared to Earth) based on actual flight environmental monitoring. HC mice were shipped to Scripps Institute just prior to the return of the Flight mice so that all mice could be dissected together in matching conditions (+/- 1 day). The mice from the Flight group were returned alive to Earth on 1/14/2019 after 39.5 days on the ISS and collected 2-4 days after splashdown following functional assays at Scripps Research Institute. In this study, fresh organ samples were obtained and immediately processed from 8 live mice that arrived at Stanford University from Scripps Research Institute on 1/16/2019. Two mice each from the following groups were included: Flight 3mo, Flight 8mo, HC 3mo, HC 8mo. All four Flight mice were dissected on 1/16/2019 to minimize time spent outside of microgravity, and all four HC mice dissected on 1/17/2019. All mice were adapted to NASA Nutrient Food Bars, four weeks prior to launch, and bars were exchanged weekly. Mice had ad libitum access to both food and water.

The optic nerves and retina were digested for 15 mins in papain and subsequently resuspended in HBSS solution for mechanical dissociation of single cells by pipetting. The corneal tissue was incubated in Dispase II for an hour with shaking followed by 10 mins of 0.25% trypsin digestion. The corneal cells were then mechanically dissociated using pipetting and resuspended in PBS (with 1% FBS). The lens tissue was processed in 0.02% EDTA for 10 mins and mechanically resuspended into single cells by pipetting. The extraocular muscles were treated with 1mg/ml collagenase for 45mins with pipetting every 15 mins for single cell suspension. All the pooled cells were finally resuspended in 1% FBS containing PBS at a concentration of 106 cells/ml for subsequent processing on 10X.  Femurs, hip bones and vertebral columns were dissected and cleaned of soft tissue. Bones were then processed as previously described (https://doi.org:10.1016/j.cell.2014.12.002, https://doi.org:10.1038/nprot.2018.041). Briefly, bones were crushed using mortar and pestle and subsequently digested in M199 (cat#11150067, Thermo Fisher Scientific) with 2.2 mg ml-1 collagenase II buffer (cat#C6885, Sigma-Aldrich) at 37 Â°C for 60 min under constant agitation. Dissociated cells were strained through a 100-Î¼m nylon filter, washed in staining medium (10% fetal bovine serum (FBS) in PBS) and pelleted at 200g at 4Â°C. The cell pellet was resuspended in staining medium and red blood cells were depleted via ACK lysis for 3 min. After an additional wash step cells were pelleted at 200g at 4Â°C. The single cell suspension was then prepared for fluorescence activated cell sorting (FACS) by staining them with fluorochrome-conjugated antibodies (Thermo Fisher Scientific) against CD45 (cat#15-0451; 1:200), TER119 (cat#15-5921; 1:200), CD51 (cat#12-0512; 1:50), Tie2 (cat#14-5987; 1:20), CD31 (cat#11-0311;1:200), Th1.1 (cat#47-0900; 1:100), Thy1.2 (47-0902; 1:100), 6c3 (cat#17-5891; 1:100), CD105 (cat#13-1051; 1:50) and streptavidinâPEâCy7 conjugate (cat#25-4317-82; 1:100). Target populations were sorted on a FACS Aria II Instrument (BD BioSciences) using a 70-Î¼m nozzle in the Shared FACS Facility in the Lokey Stem Cell Institute (Stanford). 16 Gating of cell populations was guided by appropriate isotype and fluorescence-minus- one controls. Propidium iodide staining was used to separate dead cells. Cells were sorted into staining medium and directly processed for 10X Genomics scRNA-seq.  All other tissues were processed as previously described (https://doi.org:10.1038/s41586-020-2496-1).
!Sample_extract_protocol_ch1 = Single cells were captured in droplet emulsions using the GemCode Single-Cell Instrument (10x Genomics) and scRNA-seq libraries were constructed as per the 10x Genomics protocol using GemCode Single-Cell 3â Gel Bead and Library v3 Kit. Cells were loaded in each channel with a target output of up to 5,000 cells per sample, though fewer cells were captured for small sample types. All reactions were performed in the Biorad C1000 Touch Thermal cycler with 96-Deep Well Reaction Module. Twelve cycles were used for cDNA amplification and sample index PCR. Amplified cDNA and final libraries were evaluated on a Fragment Analyzer using a High Sensitivity NGS Analysis Kit (Advanced Analytical). Library preparation was performed one organ type at a time, in sets of 8 samples. Within each organ set, cDNA was normalized and 13-20 PCR cycles run depending on cDNA amount. The average fragment length of 10x cDNA libraries was quantitated on a Fragment Analyzer (AATI), and by qPCR with the Kapa Library Quantification kit for Illumina. Each library was diluted to 4nM, and equal volumes were pooled for each NovaSeq sequencing run. Pools were sequenced with 100 cycle run kits with 28 bases for Read 1, 8 bases for Index 1, and 91 bases for Read 2 (Illumina 20012862). A PhiX control library was spiked in at 0.2 to 1%. Libraries were sequenced on the NovaSeq 6000 Sequencing System (Illumina).

!Sample_growth_protocol_ch1 = Rodent Research Reference Mission 1 (RRR-1) / Rodent Research-8 (RR-8) consisted of 40 BALB/cAnNTac females (8 used for this study) termed Flight which were sent on 12/5/2018 to the International Space Station (ISS), and a control group of 40 mice remained on Earth, termed Habitat Ground Control (HC). Furthermore, two age groups were used, younger (â¼3 months) and older (â¼8 months). Flight mice were housed at double density on launch and again during the return to earth. HC mice were housed to match, as closely as possible, conditions experienced by Flight mice. This included double density housing in identical Mouse Habitat Units and Transporters as used by NASA during launch for Flight mice, and matched temperature, humidity, and carbon dioxide levels (elevated on the ISS compared to Earth) based on actual flight environmental monitoring. HC mice were shipped to Scripps Institute just prior to the return of the Flight mice so that all mice could be dissected together in matching conditions (+/- 1 day). The mice from the Flight group were returned alive to Earth on 1/14/2019 after 39.5 days on the ISS and collected 2-4 days after splashdown following functional assays at Scripps Research Institute. In this study, fresh organ samples were obtained and immediately processed from 8 live mice that arrived at Stanford University from Scripps Research Institute on 1/16/2019. Two mice each from the following groups were included: Flight 3mo, Flight 8mo, HC 3mo, HC 8mo. All four Flight mice were dissected on 1/16/2019 to minimize time spent outside of microgravity, and all four HC mice dissected on 1/17/2019. All mice were adapted to NASA Nutrient Food Bars, four weeks prior to launch, and bars were exchanged weekly. Mice had ad libitum access to both food and water.

Red blood cells were depleted with Histopaque-1119 (SigmaAldrich RNBF0417). The cell suspension was then pelleted (300 x g, 4o C, 5 min), filtered through a 70 Î¼m strainer, and resuspended in FACS buffer (2% sterile FBS in PBS) with 100 U/mL DNase I (Worthington LS006344) prior to loading cells on a 10x chromium chip.  Murine eyes were collected carefully using forceps in cold PBS. The whole eyes from each donor were weighed. Subsequently, each of the eyes was dissected under a dissecting microscope to segregate the extraocular muscles, retina, cornea, lens and optic nerve tissue components. Each of these tissues for each donor were digested separately for single cell preparation and pooled together as eye cell suspension. The optic nerves and retina were digested for 15 mins in papain and subsequently resuspended in HBSS solution for mechanical dissociation of single cells by pipetting. The corneal tissue was incubated in Dispase II for an hour with shaking followed by 10 mins of 0.25% trypsin digestion. The corneal cells were then mechanically dissociated using pipetting and resuspended in PBS (with 1% FBS). The lens tissue was processed in 0.02% EDTA for 10 mins and mechanically resuspended into single cells by pipetting. The extraocular muscles were treated with 1mg/ml collagenase for 45mins with pipetting every 15 mins for single cell suspension. All the pooled cells were finally resuspended in 1% FBS containing PBS at a concentration of 106 cells/ml for subsequent processing on 10X.  Femurs, hip bones and vertebral columns were dissected and cleaned of soft tissue. Bones were then processed as previously described (https://doi.org:10.1016/j.cell.2014.12.002, https://doi.org:10.1038/nprot.2018.041). Briefly, bones were crushed using mortar and pestle and subsequently digested in M199 (cat#11150067, Thermo Fisher Scientific) with 2.2 mg ml-1 collagenase II buffer (cat#C6885, Sigma-Aldrich) at 37 Â°C for 60 min under constant agitation. Dissociated cells were strained through a 100-Î¼m nylon filter, washed in staining medium (10% fetal bovine serum (FBS) in PBS) and pelleted at 200g at 4Â°C. The cell pellet was resuspended in staining medium and red blood cells were depleted via ACK lysis for 3 min. After an additional wash step cells were pelleted at 200g at 4Â°C. The single cell suspension was then prepared for fluorescence activated cell sorting (FACS) by staining them with fluorochrome-conjugated antibodies (Thermo Fisher Scientific) against CD45 (cat#15-0451; 1:200), TER119 (cat#15-5921; 1:200), CD51 (cat#12-0512; 1:50), Tie2 (cat#14-5987; 1:20), CD31 (cat#11-0311;1:200), Th1.1 (cat#47-0900; 1:100), Thy1.2 (47-0902; 1:100), 6c3 (cat#17-5891; 1:100), CD105 (cat#13-1051; 1:50) and streptavidinâPEâCy7 conjugate (cat#25-4317-82; 1:100). Target populations were sorted on a FACS Aria II Instrument (BD BioSciences) using a 70-Î¼m nozzle in the Shared FACS Facility in the Lokey Stem Cell Institute (Stanford). 16 Gating of cell populations was guided by appropriate isotype and fluorescence-minus- one controls. Propidium iodide staining was used to separate dead cells. Cells were sorted into staining medium and directly processed for 10X Genomics scRNA-seq.  All other tissues were processed as previously described (https://doi.org:10.1038/s41586-020-2496-1).
!Sample_extract_protocol_ch1 = Single cells were captured in droplet emulsions using the GemCode Single-Cell Instrument (10x Genomics) and scRNA-seq libraries were constructed as per the 10x Genomics protocol using GemCode Single-Cell 3â Gel Bead and Library v3 Kit. Cells were loaded in each channel with a target output of up to 5,000 cells per sample, though fewer cells were captured for small sample types. All reactions were performed in the Biorad C1000 Touch Thermal cycler with 96-Deep Well Reaction Module. Twelve cycles were used for cDNA amplification and sample index PCR. Amplified cDNA and final libraries were evaluated on a Fragment Analyzer using a High Sensitivity NGS Analysis Kit (Advanced Analytical). Library preparation was performed one organ type at a time, in sets of 8 samples. Within each organ set, cDNA was normalized and 13-20 PCR cycles run depending on cDNA amount. The average fragment length of 10x cDNA libraries was quantitated on a Fragment Analyzer (AATI), and by qPCR with the Kapa Library Quantification kit for Illumina. Each library was diluted to 4nM, and equal volumes were pooled for each NovaSeq sequencing run. Pools were sequenced with 100 cycle run kits with 28 bases for Read 1, 8 bases for Index 1, and 91 bases for Read 2 (Illumina 20012862). A PhiX control library was spiked in at 0.2 to 1%. Libraries were sequenced on the NovaSeq 6000 Sequencing System (Illumina).
!Sample_description = Library name: SCAT-HC_2_2-Mouse_1-Pool_1
!Sample_data_processing = The obtained reads were mapped to the mm10 reference genome using cellranger (version 5.0.0, 10X Genomics). Ambient cell free mRNA contamination of each sample was removed using SoupX (version 1.5.2). Samples with more than 10% estimated contamination were removed. Raw gene counts were loaded into Seurat (version 4.0.3) for further processing. Cells with less than 200 or more than 2500 features, as well as cells with more than 50% mitochondrial RNA were removed. Samples with less than 50 cells were removed from the dataset. Finally, doublets were removed using DoubletFinder (version 2.0.3).

!Sample_growth_protocol_ch1 = Rodent Research Reference Mission 1 (RRR-1) / Rodent Research-8 (RR-8) consisted of 40 BALB/cAnNTac females (8 used for this study) termed Flight which were sent on 12/5/2018 to the International Space Station (ISS), and a control group of 40 mice remained on Earth, termed Habitat Ground Control (HC). Furthermore, two age groups were used, younger (â¼3 months) and older (â¼8 months). Flight mice were housed at double density on launch and again during the return to earth. HC mice were housed to match, as closely as possible, conditions experienced by Flight mice. This included double density housing in identical Mouse Habitat Units and Transporters as used by NASA during launch for Flight mice, and matched temperature, humidity, and carbon dioxide levels (elevated on the ISS compared to Earth) based on actual flight environmental monitoring. HC mice were shipped to Scripps Institute just prior to the return of the Flight mice so that all mice could be dissected together in matching conditions (+/- 1 day). The mice from the Flight group were returned alive to Earth on 1/14/2019 after 39.5 days on the ISS and collected 2-4 days after splashdown following functional assays at Scripps Research Institute. In this study, fresh organ samples were obtained and immediately processed from 8 live mice that arrived at Stanford University from Scripps Research Institute on 1/16/2019. Two mice each from the following groups were included: Flight 3mo, Flight 8mo, HC 3mo, HC 8mo. All four Flight mice were dissected on 1/16/2019 to minimize time spent outside of microgravity, and all four HC mice dissected on 1/17/2019. All mice were adapted to NASA Nutrient Food Bars, four weeks prior to launch, and bars were exchanged weekly. Mice had ad libitum access to both food and water.

In this study, fresh organ samples were obtained and immediately processed from 8 live mice that arrived at Stanford University from Scripps Research Institute on 1/16/2019. Two mice each from the following groups were included: Flight 3mo, Flight 8mo, HC 3mo, HC 8mo. All four Flight mice were dissected on 1/16/2019 to minimize time spent outside of microgravity, and all four HC mice dissected on 1/17/2019. All mice were adapted to NASA Nutrient Food Bars, four weeks prior to launch, and bars were exchanged weekly. Mice had ad libitum access to both food and water.

!Sample_extract_protocol_ch1 = Peripheral blood samples (0.5 â 1 mL) were collected by cardiac puncture into K2/EDTA-coated syringes and MiniCollect tubes (Greiner Bio-One) immediately after mice were euthanized by CO2 inhalation and cervical dislocation. Red blood cells were depleted with Histopaque-1119 (SigmaAldrich RNBF0417). The cell suspension was then pelleted (300 x g, 4o C, 5 min), filtered through a 70 Î¼m strainer, and resuspended in FACS buffer (2% sterile FBS in PBS) with 100 U/mL DNase I (Worthington LS006344) prior to loading cells on a 10x chromium chip.  Murine eyes were collected carefully using forceps in cold PBS. The whole eyes from each donor were weighed. Subsequently, each of the eyes was dissected under a dissecting microscope to segregate the extraocular muscles, retina, cornea, lens and optic nerve tissue components. Each of these tissues for each donor were digested separately for single cell preparation and pooled together as eye cell suspension. The optic nerves and retina were digested for 15 mins in papain and subsequently resuspended in HBSS solution for mechanical dissociation of single cells by pipetting. The corneal tissue was incubated in Dispase II for an hour with shaking followed by 10 mins of 0.25% trypsin digestion. The corneal cells were then mechanically dissociated using pipetting and resuspended in PBS (with 1% FBS). The lens tissue was processed in 0.02% EDTA for 10 mins and mechanically resuspended into single cells by pipetting. The extraocular muscles were treated with 1mg/ml collagenase for 45mins with pipetting every 15 mins for single cell suspension. All the pooled cells were finally resuspended in 1% FBS containing PBS at a concentration of 106 cells/ml for subsequent processing on 10X.  Femurs, hip bones and vertebral columns were dissected and cleaned of soft tissue. Bones were then processed as previously described (https://doi.org:10.1016/j.cell.2014.12.002, https://doi.org:10.1038/nprot.2018.041). Briefly, bones were crushed using mortar and pestle and subsequently digested in M199 (cat#11150067, Thermo Fisher Scientific) with 2.2 mg ml-1 collagenase II buffer (cat#C6885, Sigma-Aldrich) at 37 Â°C for 60 min under constant agitation. Dissociated cells were strained through a 100-Î¼m nylon filter, washed in staining medium (10% fetal bovine serum (FBS) in PBS) and pelleted at 200g at 4Â°C. The cell pellet was resuspended in staining medium and red blood cells were depleted via ACK lysis for 3 min. After an additional wash step cells were pelleted at 200g at 4Â°C. The single cell suspension was then prepared for fluorescence activated cell sorting (FACS) by staining them with fluorochrome-conjugated antibodies (Thermo Fisher Scientific) against CD45 (cat#15-0451; 1:200), TER119 (cat#15-5921; 1:200), CD51 (cat#12-0512; 1:50), Tie2 (cat#14-5987; 1:20), CD31 (cat#11-0311;1:200), Th1.1 (cat#47-0900; 1:100), Thy1.2 (47-0902; 1:100), 6c3 (cat#17-5891; 1:100), CD105 (cat#13-1051; 1:50) and streptavidinâPEâCy7 conjugate (cat#25-4317-82; 1:100). Target populations were sorted on a FACS Aria II Instrument (BD BioSciences) using a 70-Î¼m nozzle in the Shared FACS Facility in the Lokey Stem Cell Institute (Stanford). 16 Gating of cell populations was guided by appropriate isotype and fluorescence-minus- one controls. Propidium iodide staining was used to separate dead cells. Cells were sorted into staining medium and directly processed for 10X Genomics scRNA-seq.  All other tissues were processed as previously described (https://doi.org:10.1038/s41586-020-2496-1).
!Sample_extract_protocol_ch1 = Single cells were captured in droplet emulsions using the GemCode Single-Cell Instrument (10x Genomics) and scRNA-seq libraries were constructed as per the 10x Genomics protocol using GemCode Single-Cell 3â Gel Bead and Library v3 Kit. Cells were loaded in each channel with a target output of up to 5,000 cells per sample, though fewer cells were captured for small sample types. All reactions were performed in the Biorad C1000 Touch Thermal cycler with 96-Deep Well Reaction Module. Twelve cycles were used for cDNA amplification and sample index PCR. Amplified cDNA and final libraries were evaluated on a Fragment Analyzer using a High Sensitivity NGS Analysis Kit (Advanced Analytical). Library preparation was performed one organ type at a time, in sets of 8 samples. Within each organ set, cDNA was normalized and 13-20 PCR cycles run depending on cDNA amount. The average fragment length of 10x cDNA libraries was quantitated on a Fragment Analyzer (AATI), and by qPCR with the Kapa Library Quantification kit for Illumina. Each library was diluted to 4nM, and equal volumes were pooled for each NovaSeq sequencing run. Pools were sequenced with 100 cycle run kits with 28 bases for Read 1, 8 bases for Index 1, and 91 bases for Read 2 (Illumina 20012862). A PhiX control library was spiked in at 0.2 to 1%. Libraries were sequenced on the NovaSeq 6000 Sequencing System (Illumina).
!Sample_description = Library name: SCAT-HC_2_2-Mouse_4-Pool_1
!Sample_data_processing = The obtained reads were mapped to the mm10 reference genome using cellranger (version 5.0.0, 10X Genomics). Ambient cell free mRNA contamination of each sample was removed using SoupX (version 1.5.2). Samples with more than 10% estimated contamination were removed. Raw gene counts were loaded into Seurat (version 4.0.3) for further processing. Cells with less than 200 or more than 2500 features, as well as cells with more than 50% mitochondrial RNA were removed. Samples with less than 50 cells were removed from the dataset. Finally, doublets were removed using DoubletFinder (version 2.0.3).

!Sample_growth_protocol_ch1 = Rodent Research Reference Mission 1 (RRR-1) / Rodent Research-8 (RR-8) consisted of 40 BALB/cAnNTac females (8 used for this study) termed Flight which were sent on 12/5/2018 to the International Space Station (ISS), and a control group of 40 mice remained on Earth, termed Habitat Ground Control (HC). Furthermore, two age groups were used, younger (â¼3 months) and older (â¼8 months). Flight mice were housed at double density on launch and again during the return to earth. HC mice were housed to match, as closely as possible, conditions experienced by Flight mice. This included double density housing in identical Mouse Habitat Units and Transporters as used by NASA during launch for Flight mice, and matched temperature, humidity, and carbon dioxide levels (elevated on the ISS compared to Earth) based on actual flight environmental monitoring. HC mice were shipped to Scripps Institute just prior to the return of the Flight mice so that all mice could be dissected together in matching conditions (+/- 1 day). The mice from the Flight group were returned alive to Earth on 1/14/2019 after 39.5 days on the ISS and collected 2-4 days after splashdown following functional assays at Scripps Research Institute. In this study, fresh organ samples were obtained and immediately processed from 8 live mice that arrived at Stanford University from Scripps Research Institute on 1/16/2019. Two mice each from the following groups were included: Flight 3mo, Flight 8mo, HC 3mo, HC 8mo. All four Flight mice were dissected on 1/16/2019 to minimize time spent outside of microgravity, and all four HC mice dissected on 1/17/2019. All mice were adapted to NASA Nutrient Food Bars, four weeks prior to launch, and bars were exchanged weekly. Mice had ad libitum access to both food and water.
!Sample_molecule_ch1 = polyA RNA
!Sample_extract_protocol_ch1 = Peripheral blood samples (0.5 â 1 mL) were collected by cardiac puncture into K2/EDTA-coated syringes and MiniCollect tubes (Greiner Bio-One) immediately after mice were euthanized by CO2 inhalation and cervical dislocation. Red blood cells were depleted with Histopaque-1119 (SigmaAldrich RNBF0417). The cell suspension was then pelleted (300 x g, 4o C, 5 min), filtered through a 70 Î¼m strainer, and resuspended in FACS buffer (2% sterile FBS in PBS) with 100 U/mL DNase I (Worthington LS006344) prior to loading cells on a 10x chromium chip.  Murine eyes were collected carefully using forceps in cold PBS. The whole eyes from each donor were weighed. Subsequently, each of the eyes was dissected under a dissecting microscope to segregate the extraocular muscles, retina, cornea, lens and optic nerve tissue components. Each of these tissues for each donor were digested separately for single cell preparation and pooled together as eye cell suspension. The optic nerves and retina were digested for 15 mins in papain and subsequently resuspended in HBSS solution for mechanical dissociation of single cells by pipetting. The corneal tissue was incubated in Dispase II for an hour with shaking followed by 10 mins of 0.25% trypsin digestion. The corneal cells were then mechanically dissociated using pipetting and resuspended in PBS (with 1% FBS). The lens tissue was processed in 0.02% EDTA for 10 mins and mechanically resuspended into single cells by pipetting. The extraocular muscles were treated with 1mg/ml collagenase for 45mins with pipetting every 15 mins for single cell suspension. All the pooled cells were finally resuspended in 1% FBS containing PBS at a concentration of 106 cells/ml for subsequent processing on 10X.  Femurs, hip bones and vertebral columns were dissected and cleaned of soft tissue. Bones were then processed as previously described (https://doi.org:10.1016/j.cell.2014.12.002, https://doi.org:10.1038/nprot.2018.041). Briefly, bones were crushed using mortar and pestle and subsequently digested in M199 (cat#11150067, Thermo Fisher Scientific) with 2.2 mg ml-1 collagenase II buffer (cat#C6885, Sigma-Aldrich) at 37 Â°C for 60 min under constant agitation. Dissociated cells were strained through a 100-Î¼m nylon filter, washed in staining medium (10% fetal bovine serum (FBS) in PBS) and pelleted at 200g at 4Â°C. The cell pellet was resuspended in staining medium and red blood cells were depleted via ACK lysis for 3 min. After an additional wash step cells were pelleted at 200g at 4Â°C. The single cell suspension was then prepared for fluorescence activated cell sorting (FACS) by staining them with fluorochrome-conjugated antibodies (Thermo Fisher Scientific) against CD45 (cat#15-0451; 1:200), TER119 (cat#15-5921; 1:200), CD51 (cat#12-0512; 1:50), Tie2 (cat#14-5987; 1:20), CD31 (cat#11-0311;1:200), Th1.1 (cat#47-0900; 1:100), Thy1.2 (47-0902; 1:100), 6c3 (cat#17-5891; 1:100), CD105 (cat#13-1051; 1:50) and streptavidinâPEâCy7 conjugate (cat#25-4317-82; 1:100). Target populations were sorted on a FACS Aria II Instrument (BD BioSciences) using a 70-Î¼m nozzle in the Shared FACS Facility in the Lokey Stem Cell Institute (Stanford). 16 Gating of cell populations was guided by appropriate isotype and fluorescence-minus- one controls. Propidium iodide staining was used to separate dead cells. Cells were sorted into staining medium and directly processed for 10X Genomics scRNA-seq.  All other tissues were processed as previously described (https://doi.org:10.1038/s41586-020-2496-1).
!Sample_extract_protocol_ch1 = Single cells were captured in droplet emulsions using the GemCode Single-Cell Instrument (10x Genomics) and scRNA-seq libraries were constructed as per the 10x Genomics protocol using GemCode Single-Cell 3â Gel Bead and Library v3 Kit. Cells were loaded in each channel with a target output of up to 5,000 cells per sample, though fewer cells were captured for small sample types. All reactions were performed in the Biorad C1000 Touch Thermal cycler with 96-Deep Well Reaction Module. Twelve cycles were used for cDNA amplification and sample index PCR. Amplified cDNA and final libraries were evaluated on a Fragment Analyzer using a High Sensitivity NGS Analysis Kit (Advanced Analytical). Library preparation was performed one organ type at a time, in sets of 8 samples. Within each organ set, cDNA was normalized and 13-20 PCR cycles run depending on cDNA amount. The average fragment length of 10x cDNA libraries was quantitated on a Fragment Analyzer (AATI), and by qPCR with the Kapa Library Quantification kit for Illumina. Each library was diluted to 4nM, and equal volumes were pooled for each NovaSeq sequencing run. Pools were sequenced with 100 cycle run kits with 28 bases for Read 1, 8 bases for Index 1, and 91 bases for Read 2 (Illumina 20012862). A PhiX control library was spiked in at 0.2 to 1%. Libraries were sequenced on the NovaSeq 6000 Sequencing System (Illumina).
!Sample_description = Library name: SCAT-LAR_2_5-Mouse_3-Pool_1
!Sample_data_processing = The obtained reads were mapped to the mm10 reference genome using cellranger (version 5.0.0, 10X Genomics). Ambient cell free mRNA contamination of each sample was removed using SoupX (version 1.5.2). Samples with more than 10% estimated contamination were removed. Raw gene counts were loaded into Seurat (version 4.0.3) for further processing. Cells with less than 200 or more than 2500 features, as well as cells with more than 50% mitochondrial RNA were removed. Samples with less than 50 cells were removed from the dataset. Finally, doublets were removed using DoubletFinder (version 2.0.3).

!Sample_characteristics_ch1 = strain: BALB/cAnNTac
!Sample_characteristics_ch1 = Sex: female
!Sample_characteristics_ch1 = batch: Pool 3
!Sample_characteristics_ch1 = tissue: Skeletal_Stem_Cells
!Sample_characteristics_ch1 = age: 8
!Sample_characteristics_ch1 = treatment: control
!Sample_growth_protocol_ch1 = Rodent Research Reference Mission 1 (RRR-1) / Rodent Research-8 (RR-8) consisted of 40 BALB/cAnNTac females (8 used for this study) termed Flight which were sent on 12/5/2018 to the International Space Station (ISS), and a control group of 40 mice remained on Earth, termed Habitat Ground Control (HC). Furthermore, two age groups were used, younger (â¼3 months) and older (â¼8 months). Flight mice were housed at double density on launch and again during the return to earth. HC mice were housed to match, as closely as possible, conditions experienced by Flight mice. This included double density housing in identical Mouse Habitat Units and Transporters as used by NASA during launch for Flight mice, and matched temperature, humidity, and carbon dioxide levels (elevated on the ISS compared to Earth) based on actual flight environmental monitoring. HC mice were shipped to Scripps Institute just prior to the return of the Flight mice so that all mice could be dissected together in matching conditions (+/- 1 day). The mice from the Flight group were returned alive to Earth on 1/14/2019 after 39.5 days on the ISS and collected 2-4 days after splashdown following functional assays at Scripps Research Institute. In this study, fresh organ samples were obtained and immediately processed from 8 live mice that arrived at Stanford University from Scripps Research Institute on 1/16/2019. Two mice each from the following groups were included: Flight 3mo, Flight 8mo, HC 3mo, HC 8mo. All four Flight mice were dissected on 1/16/2019 to minimize time spent outside of microgravity, and all four HC mice dissected on 1/17/2019. All mice were adapted to NASA Nutrient Food Bars, four weeks prior to launch, and bars were exchanged weekly. Mice had ad libitum access to both food and water.
!Sample_molecule_ch1 = polyA RNA
!Sample_extract_protocol_ch1 = Peripheral blood samples (0.5 â 1 mL) were collected by cardiac puncture into K2/EDTA-coated syringes and MiniCollect tubes (Greiner Bio-One) immediately after mice were euthanized by CO2 inhalation and cervical dislocation. Red blood cells were depleted with Histopaque-1119 (SigmaAldrich RNBF0417). The cell suspension was then pelleted (300 x g, 4o C, 5 min), filtered through a 70 Î¼m strainer, and resuspended in FACS buffer (2% sterile FBS in PBS) with 100 U/mL DNase I (Worthington LS006344) prior to loading cells on a 10x chromium chip.  Murine eyes were collected carefully using forceps in cold PBS. The whole eyes from each donor were weighed. Subsequently, each of the eyes was dissected under a dissecting microscope to segregate the extraocular muscles, retina, cornea, lens and optic nerve tissue components. Each of these tissues for each donor were digested separately for single cell preparation and pooled together as eye cell suspension. The optic nerves and retina were digested for 15 mins in papain and subsequently resuspended in HBSS solution for mechanical dissociation of single cells by pipetting. The corneal tissue was incubated in Dispase II for an hour with shaking followed by 10 mins of 0.25% trypsin digestion. The corneal cells were then mechanically dissociated using pipetting and resuspended in PBS (with 1% FBS). The lens tissue was processed in 0.02% EDTA for 10 mins and mechanically resuspended into single cells by pipetting. The extraocular muscles were treated with 1mg/ml collagenase for 45mins with pipetting every 15 mins for single cell suspension. All the pooled cells were finally resuspended in 1% FBS containing PBS at a concentration of 106 cells/ml for subsequent processing on 10X.  Femurs, hip bones and vertebral columns were dissected and cleaned of soft tissue. Bones were then processed as previously described (https://doi.org:10.1016/j.cell.2014.12.002, https://doi.org:10.1038/nprot.2018.041). Briefly, bones were crushed using mortar and pestle and subsequently digested in M199 (cat#11150067, Thermo Fisher Scientific) with 2.2 mg ml-1 collagenase II buffer (cat#C6885, Sigma-Aldrich) at 37 Â°C for 60 min under constant agitation. Dissociated cells were strained through a 100-Î¼m nylon filter, washed in staining medium (10% fetal bovine serum (FBS) in PBS) and pelleted at 200g at 4Â°C. The cell pellet was resuspended in staining medium and red blood cells were depleted via ACK lysis for 3 min. After an additional wash step cells were pelleted at 200g at 4Â°C. The single cell suspension was then prepared for fluorescence activated cell sorting (FACS) by staining them with fluorochrome-conjugated antibodies (Thermo Fisher Scientific) against CD45 (cat#15-0451; 1:200), TER119 (cat#15-5921; 1:200), CD51 (cat#12-0512; 1:50), Tie2 (cat#14-5987; 1:20), CD31 (cat#11-0311;1:200), Th1.1 (cat#47-0900; 1:100), Thy1.2 (47-0902; 1:100), 6c3 (cat#17-5891; 1:100), CD105 (cat#13-1051; 1:50) and streptavidinâPEâCy7 conjugate (cat#25-4317-82; 1:100). Target populations were sorted on a FACS Aria II Instrument (BD BioSciences) using a 70-Î¼m nozzle in the Shared FACS Facility in the Lokey Stem Cell Institute (Stanford). 16 Gating of cell populations was guided by appropriate isotype and fluorescence-minus- one controls. Propidium iodide staining was used to separate dead cells. Cells were sorted into staining medium and directly processed for 10X Genomics scRNA-seq.  All other tissues were processed as previously described (https://doi.org:10.1038/s41586-020-2496-1).
!Sample_extract_protocol_ch1 = Single cells were captured in droplet emulsions using the GemCode Single-Cell Instrument (10x Genomics) and scRNA-seq libraries were constructed as per the 10x Genomics protocol using GemCode Single-Cell 3â Gel Bead and Library v3 Kit. Cells were loaded in each channel with a target output of up to 5,000 cells per sample, though fewer cells were captured for small sample types. All reactions were performed in the Biorad C1000 Touch Thermal cycler with 96-Deep Well Reaction Module. Twelve cycles were used for cDNA amplification and sample index PCR. Amplified cDNA and final libraries were evaluated on a Fragment Analyzer using a High Sensitivity NGS Analysis Kit (Advanced Analytical). Library preparation was performed one organ type at a time, in sets of 8 samples. Within each organ set, cDNA was normalized and 13-20 PCR cycles run depending on cDNA amount. The average fragment length of 10x cDNA libraries was quantitated on a Fragment Analyzer (AATI), and by qPCR with the Kapa Library Quantification kit for Illumina. Each library was diluted to 4nM, and equal volumes were pooled for each NovaSeq sequencing run. Pools were sequenced with 100 cycle run kits with 28 bases for Read 1, 8 bases for Index 1, and 91 bases for Read 2 (Illumina 20012862). A PhiX control library was spiked in at 0.2 to 1%. Libraries were sequenced on the NovaSeq 6000 Sequencing System (Illumina).
!Sample_description = Library name: Skeletal_Stem_Cells-HC_3_6-Mouse_2-Pool_3
!Sample_data_processing = The obtained reads were mapped to the mm10 reference genome using cellranger (version 5.0.0, 10X Genomics). Ambient cell free mRNA contamination of each sample was removed using SoupX (version 1.5.2). Samples with more than 10% estimated contamination were removed. Raw gene counts were loaded into Seurat (version 4.0.3) for further processing. Cells with less than 200 or more than 2500 features, as well as cells with more than 50% mitochondrial RNA were removed. Samples with less than 50 cells were removed from the dataset. Finally, doublets were removed using DoubletFinder (version 2.0.3).
!Sample_data_processing = Assembly: mm10 2020 A

!Sample_data_processing = Supplementary files format and content: features.tsv:file containing the feature names (output of cellranger pipeline)
!Sample_data_processing = Supplementary files format and content: matrix.mtx:Matrix file containing the gene counts for each cell barcode (output of cellranger pipeline)

!Sample_characteristics_ch1 = treatment: spaceflight
!Sample_growth_protocol_ch1 = Rodent Research Reference Mission 1 (RRR-1) / Rodent Research-8 (RR-8) consisted of 40 BALB/cAnNTac females (8 used for this study) termed Flight which were sent on 12/5/2018 to the International Space Station (ISS), and a control group of 40 mice remained on Earth, termed Habitat Ground Control (HC). Furthermore, two age groups were used, younger (â¼3 months) and older (â¼8 months). Flight mice were housed at double density on launch and again during the return to earth. HC mice were housed to match, as closely as possible, conditions experienced by Flight mice. This included double density housing in identical Mouse Habitat Units and Transporters as used by NASA during launch for Flight mice, and matched temperature, humidity, and carbon dioxide levels (elevated on the ISS compared to Earth) based on actual flight environmental monitoring. HC mice were shipped to Scripps Institute just prior to the return of the Flight mice so that all mice could be dissected together in matching conditions (+/- 1 day). The mice from the Flight group were returned alive to Earth on 1/14/2019 after 39.5 days on the ISS and collected 2-4 days after splashdown following functional assays at Scripps Research Institute. In this study, fresh organ samples were obtained and immediately processed from 8 live mice that arrived at Stanford University from Scripps Research Institute on 1/16/2019. Two mice each from the following groups were included: Flight 3mo, Flight 8mo, HC 3mo, HC 8mo. All four Flight mice were dissected on 1/16/2019 to minimize time spent outside of microgravity, and all four HC mice dissected on 1/17/2019. All mice were adapted to NASA Nutrient Food Bars, four weeks prior to launch, and bars were exchanged weekly. Mice had ad libitum access to both food and water.
!Sample_molecule_ch1 = polyA RNA
!Sample_extract_protocol_ch1 = Peripheral blood samples (0.5 â 1 mL) were collected by cardiac puncture into K2/EDTA-coated syringes and MiniCollect tubes (Greiner Bio-One) immediately after mice were euthanized by CO2 inhalation and cervical dislocation. Red blood cells were depleted with Histopaque-1119 (SigmaAldrich RNBF0417). The cell suspension was then pelleted (300 x g, 4o C, 5 min), filtered through a 70 Î¼m strainer, and resuspended in FACS buffer (2% sterile FBS in PBS) with 100 U/mL DNase I (Worthington LS006344) prior to loading cells on a 10x chromium chip.  Murine eyes were collected carefully using forceps in cold PBS. The whole eyes from each donor were weighed. Subsequently, each of the eyes was dissected under a dissecting microscope to segregate the extraocular muscles, retina, cornea, lens and optic nerve tissue components. Each of these tissues for each donor were digested separately for single cell preparation and pooled together as eye cell suspension. The optic nerves and retina were digested for 15 mins in papain and subsequently resuspended in HBSS solution for mechanical dissociation of single cells by pipetting. The corneal tissue was incubated in Dispase II for an hour with shaking followed by 10 mins of 0.25% trypsin digestion. The corneal cells were then mechanically dissociated using pipetting and resuspended in PBS (with 1% FBS). The lens tissue was processed in 0.02% EDTA for 10 mins and mechanically resuspended into single cells by pipetting. The extraocular muscles were treated with 1mg/ml collagenase for 45mins with pipetting every 15 mins for single cell suspension. All the pooled cells were finally resuspended in 1% FBS containing PBS at a concentration of 106 cells/ml for subsequent processing on 10X.  Femurs, hip bones and vertebral columns were dissected and cleaned of soft tissue. Bones were then processed as previously described (https://doi.org:10.1016/j.cell.2014.12.002, https://doi.org:10.1038/nprot.2018.041). Briefly, bones were crushed using mortar and pestle and subsequently digested in M199 (cat#11150067, Thermo Fisher Scientific) with 2.2 mg ml-1 collagenase II buffer (cat#C6885, Sigma-Aldrich) at 37 Â°C for 60 min under constant agitation. Dissociated cells were strained through a 100-Î¼m nylon filter, washed in staining medium (10% fetal bovine serum (FBS) in PBS) and pelleted at 200g at 4Â°C. The cell pellet was resuspended in staining medium and red blood cells were depleted via ACK lysis for 3 min. After an additional wash step cells were pelleted at 200g at 4Â°C. The single cell suspension was then prepared for fluorescence activated cell sorting (FACS) by staining them with fluorochrome-conjugated antibodies (Thermo Fisher Scientific) against CD45 (cat#15-0451; 1:200), TER119 (cat#15-5921; 1:200), CD51 (cat#12-0512; 1:50), Tie2 (cat#14-5987; 1:20), CD31 (cat#11-0311;1:200), Th1.1 (cat#47-0900; 1:100), Thy1.2 (47-0902; 1:100), 6c3 (cat#17-5891; 1:100), CD105 (cat#13-1051; 1:50) and streptavidinâPEâCy7 conjugate (cat#25-4317-82; 1:100). Target populations were sorted on a FACS Aria II Instrument (BD BioSciences) using a 70-Î¼m nozzle in the Shared FACS Facility in the Lokey Stem Cell Institute (Stanford). 16 Gating of cell populations was guided by appropriate isotype and fluorescence-minus- one controls. Propidium iodide staining was used to separate dead cells. Cells were sorted into staining medium and directly processed for 10X Genomics scRNA-seq.  All other tissues were processed as previously described (https://doi.org:10.1038/s41586-020-2496-1).
!Sample_extract_protocol_ch1 = Single cells were captured in droplet emulsions using the GemCode Single-Cell Instrument (10x Genomics) and scRNA-seq libraries were constructed as per the 10x Genomics protocol using GemCode Single-Cell 3â Gel Bead and Library v3 Kit. Cells were loaded in each channel with a target output of up to 5,000 cells per sample, though fewer cells were captured for small sample types. All reactions were performed in the Biorad C1000 Touch Thermal cycler with 96-Deep Well Reaction Module. Twelve cycles were used for cDNA amplification and sample index PCR. Amplified cDNA and final libraries were evaluated on a Fragment Analyzer using a High Sensitivity NGS Analysis Kit (Advanced Analytical). Library preparation was performed one organ type at a time, in sets of 8 samples. Within each organ set, cDNA was normalized and 13-20 PCR cycles run depending on cDNA amount. The average fragment length of 10x cDNA libraries was quantitated on a Fragment Analyzer (AATI), and by qPCR with the Kapa Library Quantification kit for Illumina. Each library was diluted to 4nM, and equal volumes were pooled for each NovaSeq sequencing run. Pools were sequenced with 100 cycle run kits with 28 bases for Read 1, 8 bases for Index 1, and 91 bases for Read 2 (Illumina 20012862). A PhiX control library was spiked in at 0.2 to 1%. Libraries were sequenced on the NovaSeq 6000 Sequencing System (Illumina).
!Sample_description = Library name: Skeletal_Stem_Cells-LAR_2_8-Mouse_1-Pool_3
!Sample_data_processing = The obtained reads were mapped to the mm10 reference genome using cellranger (version 5.0.0, 10X Genomics). Ambient cell free mRNA contamination of each sample was removed using SoupX (version 1.5.2). Samples with more than 10% estimated contamination were removed. Raw gene counts were loaded into Seurat (version 4.0.3) for further processing. Cells with less than 200 or more than 2500 features, as well as cells with more than 50% mitochondrial RNA were removed. Samples with less than 50 cells were removed from the dataset. Finally, doublets were removed using DoubletFinder (version 2.0.3).
